subject: Urgent: p50-p99 divergence — coordinated customer notification & product asks
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-11T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: p99 spike and throughput dip on checkout-embed (observed 08:05 PST)

Team,

Seeing an unusual latency divergence starting ~08:05 PST for the checkout-embed routing group: p50 unchanged (~35ms), p99 increased from 480ms -> 1.09s, and overall throughput for that route is down ~18% (errors low, 0.1%). The spike correlates with a higher-than-normal tail in token decoding times on a small subset of hosts.

Quick facts:
- Window: 08:05:00 -> now (08:12)
- Affected model: rwd-model-embed-v2 (serving variant A)
- Host subset: pool-embed-az3-{12,13,14} (10% of capacity)
- Error rate: flat (no backend 5xx ramp)

Attachments: datadog-spike-snapshot.png (latency heatmap), request-sample.json (example request hitting tail), runbook-latency-checklist.pdf

Immediate asks:
1) SRE/infra: can we temporarily route BrightOps and other heavy customers on this route to the compatible quantized variant (rwd-model-embed-v2-q8) as a protective fallback? We need a quick toggle and rollback plan.
2) Product/Eng: is increasing KV cache TTL from 30s -> 5m safe for this customer segment for 4 hours? Might reduce token work.
3) CS/Sales: prep a short customer-facing note (transparent, non-technical) — target ship window 10–15 min after we have mitigation in place.

I can run a targeted rollout if we greenlight fallback routing.

Soojin
SRE — Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-11T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: p99 spike and throughput dip on checkout-embed (observed 08:05 PST)

Thanks Soojin — good catch. A few constraints and product asks from my side:

- Prioritize a customer-safe mitigation that we can both roll out and rollback in <10 minutes.
- If we use the quantized variant, we need a short QA checklist (sample queries + quality check) before Broad customer routing.
- I want to avoid a long-lived config change; set expectation to apply for a 4-hour window and then auto-revert unless we decide otherwise.

Concrete product asks:
1) Karthik — can you confirm whether increasing KV cache TTL to 5m for this routing group will introduce cache pollution risk for other workloads? If safe, we should apply scoped TTL increase to BrightOps only.
2) Eng/SRE — implement targeted route toggle for BrightOps, and if possible, apply runtime-level throttling guardrail (protective QPS cap) so we don't cascade load elsewhere.
3) CS — Marissa, please draft the customer message; keep it calm, explain mitigation, ETA to resolution, and a note about follow-up RCA.

If we get LB signoff and SRE confirms rollback path, approve the fallback routing.

-Lauren
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-11T09:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: p99 spike and throughput dip on checkout-embed (observed 08:05 PST)

On Sep 11, 2027, at 08:22, Lauren Bishop wrote:
> Thanks Soojin — good catch. A few constraints and product asks from my side:

Couple of points from Product/Runtime perspective:
- Scoped TTL increase is plausible but we need quantitative risk: give me estimated additional memory and hit/miss delta for BrightOps' traffic shape. We can probably accept 5m for a 4-hour window if it's scoped to the customer.
- Quantized fallback: quality delta for BrightOps embedding use (semantic search) is typically small for v2->v2-q8 but we need one sample run on their query set. If CS can supply 20 representative queries (or we can run synthetic), we can do the QA in ~12 minutes.
- Routing toggle: we will only sign off if rollback is trivial (single flag flip) and we have traffic mirroring to validate behavior before switch.

I can prioritize a quick QA pipeline and a migration flag. SRE, can you confirm you have a plan to mirror traffic and toggle to rwd-model-embed-v2-q8 within the next 20 minutes?

- Karthik
Director, Product
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Heidi Lane <heidi@brightops.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-11T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Brief update from Redwood: performance mitigation plan (ETA ~30–90 min)

Hi Heidi — quick update from Redwood on the spike you may have seen this morning.

We detected an unusual tail latency increase affecting a small portion of requests to the checkout-embed endpoint. Our initial investigation shows no increased errors, but a p99 rise that can impact occasional checkout calls. We have an active mitigation plan:

What we are doing now:
- Routing: temporarily directing traffic from a small number (including BrightOps) to a compatible, lower-latency variant while we confirm stability.
- Protective throttling: applying a short-term guardrail to reduce risk of cascading slowdowns.
- Monitoring & QA: validating responses against a small sample set to ensure output quality is preserved.

What to expect:
- Customer impact: you may observe occasional higher latency early in the mitigation window; overall success should reduce tail spikes. No action required from your side.
- ETA: We expect to have the mitigation fully in place within 30–90 minutes; we will send a follow-up when the mitigation completes and a second message with a preliminary root-cause once we have analysis.

We apologize for the disruption — we know this is time-sensitive and will prioritize BrightOps for follow-up and transparency. If you want a brief call, I can arrange one with our SRE lead.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-11T11:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Brief update from Redwood: performance mitigation plan (ETA ~30–90 min)

Marissa — send now. SRE: proceed with targeted toggle to rwd-model-embed-v2-q8 for BrightOps; confirm mirror run and rollback flag enabled. Karthik: we have the sample queries attached to the ticket (see linked runbook); do the QA and confirm quality delta <= 2% semantic recall drop before 12:15.

Soojin — please post a short ops note to the incident channel with exact hosts touched and expected revert time (4 hours default).

I will collect notes for the postmortem template.

Lauren
(end of thread)
